findings.claim: Core Keycloak does not enforce single use for recovery codes stored through the generic user-storage path. It leaves consuming a used code entirely to the user-storage provider, with no guidance.

verifier.reason: When recovery codes are stored via the new user-storage path in server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:115-130, authentication delegates to the storage provider's CredentialInputValidator.isValid in model/storage/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/UserCredentialManager.java:58-76, bypassing local single-use removal in services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:98-111 while services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:71-92 never consumes a used code or tracks replay. Neither server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/CredentialInputValidator.java:34-41 nor server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/CredentialInputUpdater.java:24-48 documents that providers must atomically consume recovery codes during validation.

findings.claim: RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator takes the credential returned by getCredential(), which may come from user storage, makes the allCodesUsed decision on it, and calls removeStoredCredentialById(). That method only removes local/fed-storage credentials, so the provider's copy is not removed. When local and federated credentials both exist, the authenticator inspects or removes a different credential from the one that validated.

verifier.reason: RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.java:80-88) checks allCodesUsed() and calls removeStoredCredentialById() on the credential from RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:56-62), which prefers federated user-storage credentials over stored ones, whereas UserCredentialManager.removeStoredCredentialById() (model/storage/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/UserCredentialManager.java:114-117,298-305) only deletes from userLocalStorage()/userFederatedStorage() and never removes the user-storage provider's copy. Because UserCredentialManager.isValid() (model/storage/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/UserCredentialManager.java:58-79) falls back to local CredentialProviders when the federated validator rejects an input while getCredential() unconditionally returns the federated credential first, the authenticator can inspect or remove a different credential than the one that validated when both exist.

findings.claim: When createRecoveryCodesCredential stores codes in user storage (updateCredential returns true), it returns without calling recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(), so existing local recovery-code credentials are not deleted and old codes remain valid.

verifier.reason: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125-130, createRecoveryCodesCredential returns after logging when updateCredential() returns true without calling recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential() (which deletes existing stored credentials at services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:39-40) or otherwise removing local recovery-code credentials. Because model/storage/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/UserCredentialManager.java:66-79 falls through to local CredentialInputValidator providers after the federated validator, RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid() (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:99-118) still validates old codes from any leftover local credential.

findings.claim: The test calls TestAppHelper.logout(), which relies on a refreshToken set by completeLogin(), but never calls completeLogin() after submitting the recovery code, so logout may be a no-op and leave sessions behind.

verifier.reason: In testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:255-264, testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin() constructs a fresh TestAppHelper, calls startLogin() and submits the recovery code, then calls testAppHelper.logout() (ignoring its boolean return value) without calling completeLogin(). Because refreshToken is only populated in TestAppHelper.completeLogin() (testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/util/TestAppHelper.java:70-74), logout() at line 101-103 posts to the logout endpoint without a refresh_token parameter and fails silently, leaving the session behind.
